user.title: Add an Apple TV running Cue
user.description: Open Cue on the Apple TV and turn on Settings › Connection › Home Assistant Control. Its address is shown there.

data_description.host: The Apple TV's IP address or hostname.
data_description.port: Cue's Control API port. Leave it at 7788.

token.title: Token for {name}
token.description: Paste the token from Cue › Settings › Connection › Home Assistant Control (Generate Token). Case and dashes don't matter.

reauth_confirm.title: New token for {name}
reauth_confirm.description: Cue refused the saved token, so Home Assistant stopped asking (wrong tokens lock this address out for 5 minutes). Paste the current token from Cue › Settings › Connection.

error.cannot_connect: Couldn't reach the Apple TV. Open Cue on the Apple TV, with Home Assistant Control on, and check the address.
error.invalid_auth: Cue refused that token. Check it in Cue › Settings › Connection.
error.not_lan: Cue only answers devices on its local network, and this Home Assistant isn't on it (or reaches it through a public or global IPv6 address).
error.disabled: Home Assistant Control is turned off on this Apple TV. Turn it on in Cue › Settings › Connection.
error.signed_out: Cue is signed out of Plex on this Apple TV.
error.rate_limited: Too many wrong tokens from this address. Cue will accept tries again in {retry_after} s.
error.not_cue: Something answered at that address, but it isn't Cue's Control API v1.

abort.already_configured: This Apple TV is already set up.
abort.unsupported_api: This Apple TV runs a Cue Control API version this integration doesn't speak. Update the integration.
abort.no_usable_address: The Apple TV was found, but only at a link-local IPv6 address Home Assistant can't use. Add it by its IPv4 address instead.

data_description.scan_interval: How often to ask Cue what's playing.
data_description.apple_tv_entity: This Apple TV's entity from Home Assistant's Apple TV integration. Needed to start Cue when it isn't open, and for Play Media.

not_open.message: Cue isn't open on the Apple TV.

auth_failed.message: Cue refused the token. Re-authenticate the Cue integration with the current token.

rate_limited.message: Cue is refusing this address for {retry_after} s after too many wrong tokens.

bad_media_id.message: {media_id} isn't a Plex rating key (digits, optionally prefixed by the server id and a colon).

no_apple_tv.message: Play Media needs a linked Apple TV media player. Set it in the Cue integration's options.

apple_tv_missing.message: The linked Apple TV media player {entity_id} doesn't exist.

launch_failed.message: Cue didn't come to the front on {entity_id}.

play_not_started.message: Sent {url} to Cue, but it didn't start playing within {seconds} s.

outdated_cue.title: Cue on {name} is out of date
outdated_cue.description:
Cue {version} on {name} predates the Control API's stable device id and feature list. It still works, but:

- Home Assistant keys it by IP address, so an address change breaks the entry until you update it.
- One client on this Home Assistant host with a stale token can lock every client on the host out of Cue for 5 minutes.

Update Cue on the Apple TV. This notice clears itself the next time a newer Cue answers.
